constitutional_laws.full_text_english:
THE LEBANESE CONSTITUTION
Promulgated May 23, 1926

PART ONE - FUNDAMENTAL PROVISIONS

Preamble (Introduced by Constitutional Law of September 21, 1990):
(1) Lebanon is a sovereign, free, and independent country. It is a final homeland for all its citizens.
(2) Lebanon is Arab in its identity and in its affiliation.
(3) Lebanon is a parliamentary democratic republic based on respect for public liberties.
(4) The people are the source of authority and sovereignty.
(5) The political system is established on the principle of separation of powers.
(6) The economic system is free and ensures private initiative.
(7) The even development among regions shall be a basic pillar of the unity of the state.
(8) The abolition of political confessionalism shall be a basic national goal.

Chapter One - The State and Its Territory

Article 1: Lebanon is an independent, indivisible, and sovereign state.
Article 2: No part of Lebanese territory may be alienated or ceded.
Article 3: Administrative boundaries may not be modified except by law.
Article 4: Greater Lebanon is a Republic, capital Beirut.
Article 5: The Lebanese flag has three horizontal stripes - red, white, red with green cedar.

Chapter Two - The Lebanese: Their Rights and Duties

Article 6: Lebanese nationality determined by law.
Article 7: All Lebanese are equal before the law.
Article 8: Individual liberty is guaranteed and protected.
Article 9: Absolute freedom of conscience.
Article 10: Education is free.
Article 11: Arabic is the official national language.
Article 12: Right to hold public office based on merit.
Article 13: Freedom of expression, press, assembly, association.
Article 14: Inviolability of residence.
Article 15: Rights of ownership protected.

[Complete text with all 102 articles available in consolidated version]

constitutional_laws.historical_context: The Lebanese Constitution of 1926 was promulgated during the French Mandate period. It established Lebanon as a parliamentary republic with a unique confessional power-sharing system. The original constitution created a bicameral legislature (Senate and Chamber of Deputies) and a strong presidential system. It has undergone numerous amendments to adapt to Lebanon's evolving political landscape, most significantly the 1990 amendments implementing the Taif Agreement.

CONSTITUTIONAL LAW OF OCTOBER 17, 1927

This was the first major amendment to the Lebanese Constitution of 1926.

KEY CHANGES:

Article 16: Changed from bicameral to unicameral legislature (abolished Senate)
- Original: Legislative power in two chambers (Senate and Chamber of Deputies)
- Amended: Legislative power in single body (Chamber of Deputies)

Article 22: Abrogated (originally established Senate composition)
Article 23: Abrogated (originally established Senate membership requirements)

Article 24: Modified Chamber of Deputies composition
- Added appointed deputies equal to half the number of elected deputies

Article 26: Changed "Parliament" to "Chamber of Deputies"

Article 27: Removed reference to appointment power

Article 28: Modified ministerial incompatibility rules

Article 30: Modified mandate validation procedures

Article 32: Modified session dates

Article 33: Modified extraordinary session procedures

Article 34: Modified quorum requirements

Article 35: Modified secret session procedures

Article 37: Modified no-confidence procedures

Article 38-48: Various modifications to parliamentary procedures

Article 49: Modified presidential election procedure
- Changed from election by joint parliamentary assembly to Chamber of Deputies only

Article 51-58: Modified presidential powers and legislative procedures

Article 59: Modified adjournment power

Article 60: Modified presidential responsibility provisions

Article 66-68: Modified ministerial responsibility

Article 73-75: Modified presidential election timing and procedures

Article 76-79: Modified constitutional amendment procedures

Article 80: Modified Supreme Council composition

Article 84: Modified budget procedures

Article 85: Modified extraordinary credits procedure

Article 86-87: Modified budget and audit procedures

constitutional_laws.historical_context: The 1927 amendment was the first major revision of the Lebanese Constitution. It abolished the bicameral system (Senate and Chamber of Deputies) established in the original 1926 Constitution and replaced it with a unicameral legislature. This concentrated legislative power in the Chamber of Deputies and strengthened the executive branch. The amendment reflected the French Mandate authorities' preference for a more centralized political system.

constitutional_laws.full_text_english:
CONSTITUTIONAL LAW OF MAY 8, 1929

KEY CHANGES:

Article 28: Modified provisions on deputies holding ministerial positions
- Removed restrictions on number of ministers from Chamber

Article 37: Extended no-confidence right to extraordinary sessions
- Original: Only during ordinary sessions
- Amended: During ordinary or extraordinary sessions

Article 49: Extended presidential term from 3 to 6 years
- Original: 3-year term, re-eligible after 3 years
- Amended: 6-year term, re-eligible after 6 years
- Added provisional paragraph excluding current President (abrogated 1947)

Article 55: Modified dissolution provisions
- Changed procedure for dissolving Chamber of Deputies

Article 69: Abrogated provisions on government resignation
- Original detailed provisions on government resignation abrogated
- New provisions later introduced by 1990 amendment

constitutional_laws.historical_context: The 1929 amendment extended the presidential term from three to six years, providing greater stability to the executive branch. It also modified the rules regarding deputies holding ministerial positions and extended the no-confidence procedure to extraordinary parliamentary sessions. These changes further consolidated the power of the presidency and the executive branch.

constitutional_laws.historical_context: The January 21, 1947 amendment was a major revision that removed the system of appointed deputies, making the Chamber of Deputies entirely elected. It also abrogated the remaining transitional provisions related to the French Mandate period (Articles 96-100), completing Lebanon's constitutional transition to full independence.

constitutional_laws.full_text_english: CONSTITUTIONAL LAW OF MAY 22, 1948. Article 73 amended exceptionally for President Bechara El Khoury re-election. Chamber to convene within one month of promulgation for presidential election.

key_articles.subject: Exceptional presidential election timing

constitutional_laws.historical_context: The May 22, 1948 amendment was an exceptional amendment adopted specifically to allow the re-election of President Bechara El Khoury for a second term. It modified Article 73 to allow the presidential election to be held within one month of the amendment's promulgation, bypassing the normal timing requirements. This was controversial and contributed to the political crisis that led to the 1952 'Rosewater Revolution'.

constitutional_laws.full_text_french: Loi Constitutionnelle du 24 avril 1976 - Amendment d'urgence de la guerre civile
constitutional_laws.full_text_english: CONSTITUTIONAL LAW OF APRIL 24, 1976. Article 73 amended: Presidential election to be held between one month and six months before expiration of term. Application terminated September 23, 1976. Allowed election of President Elias Sarkis during civil war.

key_articles.text_arabic: شهر واحد على الأقل وستة أشهر على الأكثر قبل انتهاء المدة - ينتهي العمل به في 23 أيلول 1976
key_articles.text_french: Un mois au moins et six mois au plus avant l'expiration du mandat - application terminée le 23 septembre 1976
key_articles.subject: Emergency presidential election timing

constitutional_laws.historical_context: The April 24, 1976 amendment was adopted during the Lebanese Civil War (1975-1990). It modified Article 73 to allow the presidential election to be held up to six months before the expiration of the incumbent president's term. This allowed for the election of President Elias Sarkis on May 8, 1976, while President Suleiman Frangieh remained in office until September 23, 1976. The amendment was explicitly temporary and terminated on that date.

constitutional_laws.full_text_english:
CONSTITUTIONAL LAW NO. 18 OF SEPTEMBER 21, 1990
Implementation of the National Accord Document (Taif Agreement)

MAJOR CONSTITUTIONAL CHANGES:

PREAMBLE: Added new preamble with 10 paragraphs affirming:
- Lebanon as sovereign, free, independent country
- Arab identity and affiliation
- Parliamentary democratic republic
- People as source of authority
- Separation, balance, and cooperation of powers
- Free economic system
- Abolition of political confessionalism as national goal
- No constitutional legitimacy for authority contradicting pact of mutual existence

Article 17: Executive power transferred from President to Council of Ministers
- Original: Executive power to President assisted by ministers
- Amended: Executive power to Council of Ministers

Article 18: Legislative initiative shared between Chamber and Council of Ministers
- Original: President and Chamber had right to propose laws
- Amended: Chamber and Council of Ministers have right to propose laws

Article 19: Constitutional Council established
- New provision establishing Constitutional Council to supervise constitutionality

Article 22: Senate provision introduced (to be established with non-confessional elections)

Article 24: Confessional representation principles established
- Equal representation between Christians and Muslims
- Proportional representation among confessional groups
- Proportional representation among geographic regions

Article 33: Extraordinary sessions require President and Prime Minister agreement

Article 44: Added provision for withdrawing confidence from Chamber President/Vice President

Article 49: Presidential powers modified
- President remains Head of State and symbol of unity
- Added: Armed forces under authority of Council of Ministers
- Added: Restrictions on judges and civil servants running for President

Article 51-58: Presidential legislative powers modified to require Council of Ministers approval

Article 54: Decisions require countersignature by Prime Minister

Article 62: Council of Ministers exercises presidential authorities during vacancy

Article 64: Prime Minister powers significantly expanded
- Head of Government and its representative
- Conducts parliamentary consultations for forming government
- Signs decree of government formation with President
- Sets Council of Ministers agenda
- Follows up administration activities

Article 65: Council of Ministers powers detailed
- Sets general policy
- Watches over execution of laws
- Appoints state employees
- Can dissolve Chamber under specific conditions
- Requires two-thirds quorum
- Basic issues require two-thirds approval

Article 69: Government resignation circumstances detailed

Article 70-72: Prime Minister included in impeachment provisions

Article 77: Constitutional amendment procedure modified
- Added provision for Council of Ministers dissolution if Chamber insists on amendment

Article 79: President must consult Council of Ministers before requesting reconsideration

Article 80: Supreme Council procedure modified

Article 85: Extraordinary credits procedure modified

Article 86: Budget procedure modified - Council of Ministers decides instead of President

Article 95: Abolition of confessionalism provisions detailed
- National Committee to be formed
- Transitional plan for abolishing confessionalism
- Grade One posts distributed equally between Christians and Muslims

constitutional_laws.historical_context: The September 21, 1990 amendment implemented the National Accord Document (Taif Agreement) of October 22, 1989, which ended the Lebanese Civil War (1975-1990). This was the most significant constitutional amendment in Lebanese history, fundamentally restructuring the political system. It transferred executive power from the President to the Council of Ministers, established the principle of equal representation between Christians and Muslims, and created a more balanced power-sharing arrangement. The amendment was negotiated under Arab auspices in Taif, Saudi Arabia, and ratified by the Lebanese Parliament on November 5, 1989.

Key provisions: Christians accept Lebanon's Arab face; Muslims recognize Lebanon's independence; Power-sharing: President (Maronite), PM (Sunni), Speaker (Shia); Parliamentary ratio 6:5 (later changed to 1:1 by Taif).

constitutional_laws.historical_context: The National Pact of 1943 was an unwritten political agreement negotiated between Lebanon's first President Bechara El Khoury (Maronite) and first Prime Minister Riad Al Solh (Sunni). It established the confessional power-sharing system that has defined Lebanese politics since independence.

constitutional_laws.historical_context: The Taif Agreement was negotiated in Taif, Saudi Arabia, from September 30 to October 22, 1989, under Arab League auspices. It ended the Lebanese Civil War (1975-1990) and fundamentally restructured Lebanon's political system. Signed by 62 Lebanese deputies and ratified November 5, 1989. Implemented constitutionally through Constitutional Law of September 21, 1990.
